subject: [hw] DONE V03
body:
V03 (ELF32/ARM loader: PT_LOAD + PT_DYNAMIC, plain REL / Android APS2 / RELR, GNU hash lookup, shims, init arrays) is implemented and host-tested. No phone, no publish.

Test command and last line:
    $ bash gpu/hwcodec/loader/test_v03/run_tests.sh
    N2TEST V03 PASS 9543/9543
(ASan+UBSan -O1 and plain -O2; 9473 llvm-readelf-oracle checks per build + 58 hand-built relocation-encoding checks. ~2 s, all builds under /tmp/n2hw-V03.)

Vendor set acceptance line printed by the test:
    V03 vendor: objects 5, relocations 3120, unresolved 146, unique imports 149
Explanation of 146 vs 149 (honest, not a shortcut): the set has 149 unique undefined symbol names; 2 are data imports (__stack_chk_guard, stderr, resolved by the test data shim table) and __aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0 has no dynamic relocation at all (only .ARM.exidx), so 146 functions are bound to named unresolved slots. Per object, applied relocations equal llvm-readelf exactly: vpud 91, libvpud_vcodec 191, libvcodecdrv 2162, utility 498, oal 178.

Implemented:
- n2elf_load: ET_DYN/EM_ARM/ELF32-LE only; PT_LOAD at a page-aligned base from n2a32_mem_alloc (bss zeroed); PT_DYNAMIC for NEEDED, SONAME, SYMTAB/STRTAB/STRSZ/SYMENT, GNU_HASH, DT_HASH (count), REL/RELSZ/RELENT, JMPREL/PLTRELSZ/PLTREL, ANDROID_REL/RELSZ, RELR 36/35/37 + Android 0x6fffe000 family, INIT, FINI, INIT_ARRAY, FINI_ARRAY, PREINIT_ARRAY; every table validated inside a PT_LOAD; protections applied only after relocation (text RO/data RW verified).
- n2elf_reloc.c: plain REL; APS2 packed with every group-flag combination (correct per-item order: offset delta then r_info; explicit addends parsed and ignored on Elf32_Rel like bionic); RELR bitmaps; R_ARM_RELATIVE/GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT/ABS32; anything else is a named error (R_ARM_PREL31 (42) tested).
- n2elf_link: GNU hash across objects in load order (global/weak/unique), then function shims via n2a32_hostcall_register, then data shims (allocate+init once), unresolved functions to named slots with a unique count, unresolved data imports are an error; incremental/no-op on a second call.
- n2elf_sym, n2elf_entry, n2elf_base, n2elf_describe, n2elf_run_init (dependency order via DT_NEEDED, preinit/init/init_array, once per object; DT_INIT tested with a patched object).
- Tests: reversed-order 4-object synthetic set covering plain REL, Android packed, packed+RELR, RELR, Thumb, weak symbols, duplicates, cross-object imports, unresolved weak import; field-by-field comparison of 3120 vendor relocations and 2593 symbols; bss/data/permissions; ET_EXEC, bad type, bad APS2, unresolved data, truncated, missing, bad FINI_ARRAY, bad RELRENT negatives; 58 encoding unit checks.

Not done / limitations (full list in STATUS):
- RELA, TLS, COPY, symbol versions (ignored per header), GNU_RELRO, unloading; FINI arrays parsed but no fini API exists. NEEDED not loaded is ignored; duplicate sonames allowed; guest memory not reclaimed on a failed load; n2elf_sym sees exported symbols only (GNU hash).
- Unresolved stop reason: intended n2a32_hostcall_register(NULL, name) (STOP_NOIMPORT + name). V02's current core rejects NULL fn at emu/n2a32_core.c:106, so n2elf.c has a fallback (shared callback per name) that stops with STOP_REQUEST, keeps stop_addr on the slot and the name recoverable. I asked hw-v02 for the one-line change; the fallback is removed when their core accepts NULL. Posted twice, no answer yet.
- Not compiled for arm64 iOS; not run on the phone. llvm-readelf 23.1.4 has no --raw-relr; -r expands RELR and agrees with the section decode.
- Manual integration against V02's current core works: vendor set links (146 unresolved); a slot call stops at 0xfff0000c with name never_defined_fn (STOP_REQUEST, see above).

Files changed (all new, owned paths): gpu/hwcodec/loader/n2elf.c, gpu/hwcodec/loader/n2elf_reloc.c, gpu/hwcodec/loader/test_v03/** (run_tests.sh, oracle.py, t_v03.c, t_reloc.c, stub/n2a32_stub.c, fixtures/*.c, STATUS.md), gpu/hwcodec/dsh-state/workers/V03/STATUS.md. No commit (tree still untracked like the other workers); no vendor file copied.
